paragraph.text: The term “agency” has the meaning given that term in section 551 of title 5.

paragraph.chapeau: The term “covered data” means information that—

subparagraph.text: identifies or is linked or reasonably linkable to an individual; and

subparagraph.chapeau: is collected, processed, or transferred by means of—

clause.text: the internet or any other digital means;
a device capable of connecting to the internet; or

clause.chapeau: any sensor or similar technology that collects—

paragraph.continuation: Such term does not include publicly available information or de-identified data.

paragraph.text: The term “Commission” means the Federal Trade Commission.

The term “transfer” means to disclose, release, disseminate, make available, sell, or license covered data, or provide access to covered data, to a third party by any means, including by providing such data to a third party in exchange for consideration, by providing interoperability with a third party, or by otherwise making such data accessible to a third party.

subsection.text: Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to limit the authority of the Commission under section 45 of title 15.

note.heading: References in Text
note.p: For definition of agency, referred to in subsec. (a)(1), see section 551 of title 5, Government Organization and Employees.

subsection.text: A covered entity may not collect, process, or transfer covered data unless such collection, processing, or transfer is limited to what is reasonably necessary and proportionate.

subsection.chapeau: A covered entity shall obtain affirmative express consent from an individual before—

paragraph.text: collecting sensitive covered data from that individual;
transferring covered data to a third party; or
using covered data for targeted advertising directed at the individual.

subsection.text: Subsection (b) shall not apply to the collection, processing, or transfer of covered data that is strictly necessary to fulfill a transaction or provide a service specifically requested by the individual.

note.heading: Effective Date
note.p: Pub. L. 119–42, § 5, Jan. 15, 2026, 140 Stat. 112, provided that: “This section shall take effect 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act [Jan. 15, 2026].”

note.heading: Regulations
note.p: Pub. L. 119–42, § 6, Jan. 15, 2026, 140 Stat. 112, provided that: “Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act [Jan. 15, 2026], the Commission shall promulgate regulations to carry out this section.”

paragraph.text: Any covered entity that violates section 102 of this title shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than $50,000 per violation.

paragraph.chapeau: The civil penalty under paragraph (1) shall be not more than $100,000 per violation if—

subparagraph.text: the violation involved the data of a minor;
the covered entity had actual knowledge of the violation; or
the violation resulted in significant harm to an individual.

subsection.text: Any individual whose covered data is collected, processed, or transferred in violation of section 102 of this title may bring a civil action in any court of competent jurisdiction.
